Based on your preference for non-fiction books focused on self-improvement and entrepreneurship, particularly those inspired by the practical habit-building strategies in 'Atomic Habits' and the iterative, customer-focused methodology of 'The Lean Startup', here are three highly recommended books:

1. **"Deep Work" by Cal Newport**
   This book complements 'Atomic Habits' by focusing on the quality of your attention rather than just the quantity of tasks completed. It provides a framework for cultivating intense focus, which is essential for entrepreneurs and professionals looking to produce high-value work in a distracted world.

2. **"Zero to One" by Peter Thiel**
   If you enjoyed the innovation and startup aspects of 'The Lean Startup', this book offers a contrasting but complementary perspective. Thiel argues for creating new things (going from 0 to 1) rather than copying what works (going from 1 to n). It is excellent for understanding monopolistic competition and long-term strategic thinking in business.

3. **"Mindset: The New Psychology of Success" by Carol S. Dweck**
   This foundational text on self-improvement explores the concept of the "growth mindset" versus the "fixed mindset." It aligns well with the philosophy of continuous improvement found in both of your favorite books, providing the psychological underpinnings for why habits change and how entrepreneurs can view failure as data rather than defeat.
